findings.quote: Direct public comparables are scarce: the peer set the pack assembles spans optical-component and broader semiconductor suppliers rather than pure directed-energy laser makers, so the peer multiples are a loose reference rather than a clean benchmark.
findings.issue: The grounding surface carries no assembled peer set and no peer multiples. The prompt Facts header reads "Multiples (company column; peers pending a peer data source)" and the report's own multiples table note reads "Peer multiples pending a peer data source." The prose nonetheless asserts a peer set exists ("the peer set the pack assembles"), characterizes its composition ("optical-component and broader semiconductor suppliers"), and treats peer multiples as usable ("a loose reference"). That is a characterization the pack does not carry and it contradicts the report's own rendered table. (For the record, the raw FactPack peers are AAOI, HIMX, JAMF, LSPD with all-null P/E, P/S and EV/EBITDA; JAMF and LSPD are software companies, so even the underlying list is not "optical-component and broader semiconductor suppliers.")
findings.fix: Drop the claim that a peer set was assembled and that peer multiples serve as a reference. State plainly that no peer comparables were available in the pack (peers pending a data source), consistent with the multiples-table note, and rest the "expensive" conclusion on the company's own P/S of 7.6x and NTM P/E of 83.1x.
findings.note: Rewrite removes the fabricated peer set. Now reads "No peer-multiple comparison is available in the pack, where peer data is pending a source, so we anchor on nLIGHT's own trading history and on the Street's targets rather than on a comparable-company set," consistent with the multiples-table note, and rests the expensive call on the grounded P/S 7.6x and NTM P/E 83.1x.

findings.quote: management points to the Department of War's Joint Laser Weapon Systems award as a template for more program wins. || management frames the Department of War's Joint Laser Weapon Systems award as a template for further directed-energy wins.
findings.issue: The same claims recur across sections in paraphrase (rubric item 7). (a) The Joint Laser Weapon Systems "template for [more/further] wins" line appears in executiveSummary.catalysts[0] and again, nearly verbatim, in growth.points[1]. (b) The ~$17M of Q3 product revenue delayed by the supply chain appears in catalysts[1], growth.points[3] and risks.idiosyncratic[0]. (c) The $305.9M/$347.1M consensus revenue path appears in catalysts[2], growth.points[2] and valuation.scenarios[1].driver. (d) The Aerospace and Defense +40.8% Q2 YoY figure appears in catalysts[0] and businessMoat.moatFactors[1]. (e) The 83.1x NTM P/E appears in executiveSummary.thesis.body and valuation.multiplesCommentary. Exec-summary catalysts should point; the body sections should argue distinct points rather than restate the pointer.
findings.fix: Give each figure one home section that states it in full, and refer back in words elsewhere. E.g. state the $17M delay once (risks) and have growth refer to "the delayed shipments noted under risks"; let growth.points[1] argue a point distinct from the catalyst rather than repeat the JLWS-template line; give the $305.9M/$347.1M consensus path a single home and point to it from the others.
findings.note: All five resolved. (a) growth.points[1] now argues 2025 A&D +60% to $175.3M, not the JLWS line (which stays only in catalysts[0]). (b) $17M stated once in risks.idiosyncratic[0]; catalysts[1] refers in words, growth.points[3] uses the distinct $63-73M Q3 range. (c) $305.9M/$347.1M homed in growth.points[2]; catalysts[2] and the Base driver refer in words. (d) +40.8% dropped from moatFactors[1]. (e) 83.1x dropped from thesis.body, kept only in multiplesCommentary.

findings.quote: as a defense-led ramp reshaped the top line and returned the company to double-digit revenue growth.
findings.issue: The five-year income series on the page shows YoY growth of -10.4% (FY22), -13.3% (FY23), -5.4% (FY24) and +31.6% (FY25), with FY21 YoY blank; it never shows a prior year of positive double-digit growth. "returned ... to double-digit revenue growth" implies a prior double-digit-growth state the series does not support (rubric item 2 / item 9).
findings.fix: Write "returned the company to growth" or "delivered double-digit revenue growth" — both supported by the series — and drop the "returned to double-digit" implication.
findings.note: Now reads "A defense-led ramp reshaped the top line in 2025 and delivered double-digit revenue growth after several years of decline." The "returned to double-digit" implication is gone; +31.6% FY25 after three down years supports the wording.

findings.quote: prompting a re-rating toward the analyst target range of $81.00 to $100.00 while the shares stay below their 52-week high of $86.95.
findings.issue: The Bull scenario's implied price is $70 and the report's target high is $68, but the Bull driver narrates a re-rating "toward the analyst target range of $81.00 to $100.00" and cites the $86.95 52-week high. Set beside a $70 implied price, the $81-100 figures read as more upside than the scenario itself carries (rubric item 6, coherence within the Bull box). The individual figures are grounded (Street range $81-100; 52-week high $86.95); the issue is internal consistency.
findings.fix: Anchor the Bull narrative to its own ~$70 implied price, or state explicitly that the bull case stops short of the Street's $81-100 range (a partial re-rating), so the driver and the implied price agree.
findings.note: Bull driver now ends "driving a partial re-rating that recovers part of the drop from the 52-week high but stops short of the Street's more bullish targets." The specific $81-100 / $86.95 figures are gone and the narrative is coherent with the $70 implied price.
